sources.citation: Westerlund, Torbjörn. 2015. A grammatical sketch of Ngarla (Ngayarta, Pama-Nyungan). Canberra: Asia-Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: OTHER LANGUAGE (neighbouring Ngarla): sec. 2.3 'main stress always falls on the first syllable of a word', secondary stress by word length. Mentions Kariyarra only as a community; no claim about Kariyarra stress.

sources.citation: Nash, David & Geoff O'Grady. 2001. Hale and O'Grady's 1960 SA and WA vocabularies. In J. Simpson et al. (eds), Forty years on: Ken Hale and Australian languages (PL 512). Canberra: Pacific Linguistics.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Documents a Kariyarra (Kariera) vocabulary taken at Roebourne, 22 March 1960 (speaker Adam Barker); no phonological statements.

sources.citation: Dench, Alan. 1995. Martuthunira: a language of the Pilbara region of Western Australia. Pacific Linguistics C-125.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: OTHER LANGUAGE: reports O'Grady et al.'s 79% Kariyarra-Ngarluma cognate figure (dialect pair); sec. 2.6 stress is for Martuthunira only; no Ngayarda-wide or Kariyarra stress claim.

sources.citation: StressTyp2 (StressTyp2-v1-archive-0415 SQL dump) and WALS CLDF (local copies)
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: No Kariyarra/Kariera entry in StressTyp2 (name appears only in an ISO code table); WALS 'Kariera' (vka) has only feature 39B, no stress features.

sources.citation: Wangka Maya Pilbara Aboriginal Language Centre. 2026. Kariyarra (language web page), https://www.wangkamaya.org.au/pilbara-languages/kariyarra
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Names the 2001 Wordlists & Sketch Grammar, a 2001 book of Kariyarra texts, and a new dictionary 'expected to be published early in 2026'; example sentences and a wordlist; no phonology or stress.

sources.citation: Thieberger, Nicholas. 1993. Handbook of Western Australian Aboriginal languages south of the Kimberley region. Pacific Linguistics C-124. Canberra: ANU.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Bibliographic handbook. Sec. 4.4.4 Kariyarra (pp.112-114): '5. People who have worked intensively to record the language: No one'; '9. Grammar or sketch grammar: None'; spelling as for Ngarluma; O'Grady et al. 1966 treat Kariera and Ngarluma (79% shared vocabulary) as dialects of one language. Nothing on stress.

sources.citation: von Brandenstein, C. G. 1967. The language situation in the Pilbara - past and present. Papers in Australian Linguistics No. 2 (PL A-11), 1-20.
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Sociolinguistic survey; the only stress remark concerns Jindjiparndi (stress shift revealing vowel length); nothing on Kariera stress.

sources.citation: Wangka Maya Pilbara Aboriginal Language Centre. n.d. Speaking, Reading & Writing Pilbara Aboriginal Languages (brochure).
sources.access_detail: a copy the project holds (available on request)
sources.note: Generic sounds/spelling/CV-syllable guide for all Pilbara languages; silent on stress.

sources.citation: Kohn, Allison. 2012. A morphological description of Ngarluma. Port Hedland: Wangka Maya PALC (and von Brandenstein, C. G. 1970. Narratives from the north-west of Western Australia in the Ngarluma and Jindjiparndi languages, 3 vols, Canberra: AIAS).
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Descriptions of Ngarluma, the sister dialect (O'Grady et al. 1966: one language with Kariera); a Ngarluma stress statement would be the fallback if no Kariyarra-specific one exists (identity caveat: ngar1287, not kari1304).

sources.citation: Gordon, Raylene et al. (Wangka Maya Pilbara Aboriginal Language Centre). 2001. Kariyarra Wordlists and Sketch Grammar. South Hedland: Wangka Maya PALC. ISBN 1875946322. 161 pp.
sources.tag: likely states stress; not yet obtained
sources.access_detail: print only (no digital copy found when the work was looked up)
sources.note: Glottolog's only descriptive work for kari1304; a Wangka Maya sketch grammar of this series normally opens with a sounds/spelling section where a stress statement would sit. Scan exists (archive.org kariyarrawordlis00rayl, 198 leaves) but is access-restricted; print copies via Wangka Maya store / AIATSIS / NLA.
